evidence.note: 'Avoid setting package default_visibility to //visibility:public'; public only on targets forming the public API.
'Avoid setting default_visibility to public... the risk of inadvertently creating public targets increases'; prefer package_group.
'it is an antipattern for a macro to declare a target with public visibility'.

bzl-public-visibility.whyNotLinter: Buildifier has no visibility warning; Bazel only errors when visibility is too narrow, never too wide.
bzl-public-visibility.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred, no study found): the shortest fix for a 'target is not visible' build error is `//visibility:public`.
bzl-public-visibility.expectedNoise: med -- 'implementation detail' is judged from names; a repo that publishes most targets should disable it.

evidence.note: Non-hermeticity sources: host binaries and absolute paths, timestamps/build ids, writing to the source tree.
'Do ensure that tools run by a genrule are deterministic and hermetic. They should not write timestamps to their output'; avoid network access.

bzl-nonhermetic-action.whyNotLinter: Buildifier does not parse `cmd` strings; the sandbox allows network by default and absolute host tools work locally, so builds pass until remote execution or another machine.
bzl-nonhermetic-action.aiRelevance: Medium (inferred): agents translate Makefile/shell habits (curl, /usr/bin/python3) into genrules.
bzl-nonhermetic-action.expectedNoise: low -- repository rules are excluded explicitly.

evidence.note: 'Any *_binary or tool to be executed by cmd must appear in this list [tools], not in srcs, to ensure they are built in the correct configuration.'

bzl-genrule-tool-in-srcs.whyNotLinter: Buildifier does not relate `cmd` usage to attributes; the build succeeds on single-platform setups and breaks only when cross-compiling or with remote exec.
bzl-genrule-tool-in-srcs.aiRelevance: Medium (inferred): passes local builds, so agents' tests never catch it.

evidence.note: Recommends enforcing sandboxing so actions only see declared inputs.
`local = True` forces local execution and bypasses sandbox/remote.

bzl-sandbox-opt-out-unexplained.whyNotLinter: The tags are literal, but they are legitimate when justified; the rule asks whether a justification exists, which needs reading comments.
bzl-sandbox-opt-out-unexplained.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred): adding `no-sandbox` is the quickest way to make a 'file not found in sandbox' error disappear.

evidence.note: 'Generated targets... should have their names prefixed by <name>', restricted visibility and a manual tag.
Symbolic macros enforce the prefix naming at load time; legacy macros do not.

bzl-macro-fixed-target-names.whyNotLinter: Buildifier `unnamed-macro` only checks that a `name` parameter exists; legacy macros are not checked for derived names.
bzl-macro-fixed-target-names.aiRelevance: Medium (inferred): agents write macros that create a fixed helper target and test with one call site only.

evidence.note: Avoid flattening depsets: 'doing so usually results in O(N^2) cost'; use ctx.actions.args() to defer expansion.

bzl-depset-flatten-in-impl.whyNotLinter: Buildifier `depset-iteration` flags implicit iteration and `overly-nested-depset` flags depsets in loops; an explicit `.to_list()` on a transitive depset is not flagged.
bzl-depset-flatten-in-impl.aiRelevance: Medium (inferred): Python-trained habits turn every collection into a list.
bzl-depset-flatten-in-impl.expectedNoise: low-med -- small local depsets are excluded.
